To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased endothelial stretch, as occurs in hypertension, promotes conversion of monocytes to intermediate monocytes and that this occurs through activation of STAT3, IL-6, and hydrogen peroxide.

hypertension promotes monocyte differentiation to intermediate monocytes and activation of STAT3 in mononuclear phagocytes in part due to increased endothelial mechanical strain and loss of nitric oxide signalling and increased release by endothelial cells of interleukin 1β, interleukin (6), hydrogen peroxide, and tumour growth factor β.
increased endothelial stretch promotes monocyte differentiation and STAT3 activation and that these effects are likely mediated by increased production of IL-6, H2O2, and loss of NO signalling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how hypertension and increased endothelial stretch promote monocyte activation and differentiation and the role of IL-6, STAT3, and hydrogen peroxide in this process.
the role of monocytes in hypertension.
the role of the vascular endothelum in the pathophysiology of hypertension, and the mechanisms by which hypertension induces atherosclerosis and renal injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

hypertension and increased mechanical stretch of the endothelium promote monocyte differentiation to intermediate and CD209-expressing monocytes, and this is mediated by IL-6, hydrogen peroxide, STAT3, and loss of NO.
hypertension and increased endothelial stretch promote monocyte conversion to intermediate monocytes via IL-6 and H2O2 and STAT3 activation.
increased endothelial stretch in hypertension is a key mediator of monocyte phenotype and functional activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypertension and increased endothelial stretch promote monocyte conversion to intermediate monocytes and their activation by STAT3, IL-6 and H2O2.
hypertension and increased endothelial stretch promote monocyte conversion to intermediate monocytes and activation.
hypertension and increased endothelial stretch can promote monocyte differentiation, activation, and recruitment to sites of vascular injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypertension promotes a shift in monocyte phenotype and activation, which may contribute to vascular and renal disease.

the endothelium plays a key role in promoting monocyte activation and differentiation in hypertension and that these processes can be modulated by interventions that enhance bioavailable NO and/or reduce the production of hydrogen peroxide and IL-6 by the endotheliam and/or inhibit STAT3 in monocyte.
endothelial dysfunction and increased mechanical stretch can promote monocyte activation, which may have important roles in the pathogenesis of hypertension and related cardiovascular disease.
